elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Revised 6.1 reads: "HDI shall be a non-exclusive provider of the services under this Agreement, and the Company shall have no exclusivity or sole-provider obligation to HDI." The prior bar on the Company participating in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products is deleted, and the grant to HDI of the exclusive right to use the Company's own "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site is likewise deleted, so no Vendor exclusive right remains that would block Customer's use of its own brand or its dealings with alternative providers. No residual requirements/sole-source language appears elsewhere in the rendered text (4.1 is term/renewal only; 6.2 is a Customer-favourable retained right).

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose premise does not apply: after the edit there is no exclusivity obligation on the Company at all, so no product-category limitation is required. The preferred outcome subsumes the fallback ceiling.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity period exists in the rendered 6.1; the auto-renewing term in 4.1 no longer carries any exclusive-dealing covenant, so the 12-month ceiling cannot be exceeded.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: there is no exclusivity to terminate, so no performance-based exit trigger is needed. (Section 1.6 launch-delay right and 4.2 Termination Payment are untouched and unaffected.)

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity obligation survives in 6.1, so no delivery-date exit mechanic is required.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete on the operative text: the single element is met by the replacement of 6.1 with an express no-exclusivity/no-sole-provider statement, including removal of HDI's exclusive right over the Customer's own "Deerskin" brand, which the rule boundary requires for a complete result.

Scope of the edit is confined to the exclusivity provision. Section 4.1 (term/auto-renewal), Section 6.2 (Customer's closeout-merchandise right) and HDI's own restrictions in 6.3 are retained unchanged, and no survival tail, expense, damages, procedure or boilerplate extras were added.

Deletion of the introductory words "Except as provided in Section 6.2" leaves no dangling cross-reference: Section 6.2 stands on its own as an affirmative retained Customer right and does not contradict the new 6.1.

Minor drafting note (not a defect): the two halves of new 6.1 ("HDI shall be a non-exclusive provider" and "the Company shall have no exclusivity or sole-provider obligation") are mutually reinforcing rather than duplicative operative obligations; neither imposes any requirement outside the checklist, so minimality is preserved.

The comment accurately states the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the 12-month category-limited performance-exit fallback without over-promising anything absent from the operative text.
